It is a robust, non‑parametric method that is well‑suited to the trend‑dominated, non‑stationary series with unstable model rankings and correlated errors, avoiding the high variance that can arise from weighted or full‑pool approaches.
decision.top3_why_not: Candidate B (DTW barycenter of the full pool) has a lower overall score but exhibits extreme variability across windows (0.7069, 0.6900, 0.5037), indicating overfitting to a single window and poor generalization. Candidate A (trimmed_mean pool1) is slightly worse (0.6696) and, while stable, does not outperform the median and may unnecessarily discard useful information by trimming 20% of the predictions. Thus, the median strategy offers the best balance of robustness and performance for this series.
decision.justification: The median combination on the stable subset (pool1) delivers the best validation score (0.6561) and shows the most consistent performance across the three validation windows (0.6728, 0.6402, 0.6869). It is a robust, non‑parametric method that is well‑suited to the trend‑dominated, non‑stationary series with unstable model rankings and correlated errors, avoiding the high variance that can arise from weighted or full‑pool approaches.
